analysis.title: Nick Savone - Global Reflections 21 Nov 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 had its worst week since Liberation Day (April 2025) and the Nasdaq Composite its worst since 2020. Nasdaq is down on the year and in technical bear-market territory after being up 18.7% on October 6. Friday was the S&P's 7th straight decline, the longest streak since February 2020.

Selling has spread well beyond AI and Tech. Weekly S&P decliners outnumbered gainers by more than 15:1, and S&P forward P/E fell to 16.5x while earnings revision breadth stays positive in the US and Europe.

Nvidia beat revenue expectations by about $7B and guided about $5B ahead, yet fell 22.7% on the week. Its forward P/E relative to the S&P is at a record low, with doubts centred on export controls, financing and AI returns.

Consumer prints were mixed. Walmart showed weaker US comps at about 40x forward earnings, Target traffic grew 5%, Ross comps were +8% but below buyside hopes, and WSM fell about 15% despite positive comps. TJX Marmaxx comps +2% vs 1% expected, and MS sees a re-rating case.

Macro signals show a growth scare while activity data stays resilient. The 2Y yield fell 24bps, copper fell 9.9%, WTI fell 5.8%, control-group retail sales beat, claims are low and Indeed postings hit a 19-month high.

The Fed is the central debate. Markets price about 62bps of further hikes over ten months. Tighter financial conditions from lower equities and a stronger dollar add restraint, and QDS says price action mirrors 2018. A change in the expected path could give relief before any formal pivot.

Asia sold off hard on Friday: Taiwan -6.2%, Korea -5.2%, Nikkei -5.1%, with KOSPI below 5,000 and over 300 Taiwan stocks limit-down. Tighter US export controls cut Alibaba FY28-29 revenue and EBITA estimates despite cloud growth guidance of 30-45% in FY28 and 50% in FY29.

Europe had its worst week since Liberation Day, with a flight to defensives. Global Staples now trade at a 73% P/E premium to IT, the largest on record, after outperforming Tech by 49% in under two months, the biggest rotation since March 2001.

New US export controls on advanced AI chips and overseas compute are more restrictive than expected. MS expects slower data center builds in Malaysia and Thailand, with US developers such as EQIX, CIFR, GLXY and RIOT preferred.
Gold is down a third from January highs, its biggest 12M drawdown since the early 1980s, with 14D RSI at a 3-year low. Higher dollar and yields weighed, even as 10Y real yields came off highs.

Hedge fund positioning is de-grossing. US L/S net leverage fell 5ppts to 41% (6th percentile since 2010) and gross fell 4ppts to 195%. Funds are net short Momentum for the first time since April 2025, and nets could drop below 40% after Friday.

MS strategists turned constructive for 2027. Wilson raised the S&P 12M target to 8,700 with EPS of $369/$420/$458 for 2026/27/28 and Industrials as top sector. Tang moved global equities to max Overweight, and Zavolock raised the MSCI Europe YE2027 target to 3,030.

MS economics views: Gapen sees US GDP 2.6% in 2026 and Fed hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.50%. Eisenschmidt sees two ECB hikes to a 3.0% deposit rate by March 2027. Yamaguchi sees two BoJ hikes to 1.75%. Xing sees China GDP slowing to 4.4% in 2027.

Sentiment is fragile. The Global Risk Demand Index fell into Fear at -2.4SD, the 8th such signal in 3M. US Defensives beat the Nasdaq by more than 25% in 6 weeks. Nvidia trades at 8.3x 12M forward P/E, a record 50% discount to SPX.

Take-Two's GTA VI launched with third-party estimates of 19M copies and $1.8B gross sales, and MS sees a scenario of 30M copies in 24 hours. SpaceX Starship Flight 15 caught the upper stage for the first time and Adam Jonas graded it an A.
Several research initiations and rating changes were flagged: E&C initiations, Nucor upgrade to OW with $310 PT, Moncler downgrade to UW, and CBOE as Top Pick.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reported revenue about $7B above expectations and guided about $5B ahead, but shares fell 22.7% on the week.
Intuit reported a strong first quarter but cut FY27 revenue outlook on Credit Karma, while holding full-year operating income and EPS guidance.
Walmart reported weaker US comps and a slowing customer funnel, with eCommerce intact. Tariff refunds and price reinvestment complicate operating income. Stock trades at about 40x forward earnings.
Target reported 5% traffic growth. Ross Stores reported 8% comps, below buyside expectations. Williams-Sonoma fell about 15% initially despite positive comps in every brand.
TJX 3Q26 reported Marmaxx comps +2% vs 1% expected, International +8%, Canada +6%, HomeGoods eighth straight quarter of MSD+ comps. 4Q guidance modestly reduced on freight and fuel costs.

Alibaba guided to cloud revenue growth of 30-45% in FY28 and 50% in FY29, but FY28-29 revenue and EBITA estimates were cut on export restrictions. PDD reported 12% online marketing revenue growth with flat total revenue.
Experian reported 7% organic revenue growth, 50bps margin expansion and an extra $500M buyback. NKT maintained FY26 operational EBITDA guidance of €400-430M, now toward the upper end.
Wilson forecasts S&P EPS of $369 in 2026, $420 in 2027 and $458 in 2028 (MS estimates).
Infineon sees AI data center demand above its €4B FY27 guide. ASM International reiterated €5.7B+ FY27 sales. Nokia AI & Cloud reached 12% of sales vs 6% a year ago.

risk_factors: Further systematic selling and fragile sentiment after repeated false dawns.
Hawkish Fed with tighter financial conditions from a stronger dollar and lower equities.
Tighter AI chip export controls and visibility beyond 2027.
French election and fiscal risks, and energy price spikes.
Gap between prices and earnings expectations, which may signal a growth problem not yet in the numbers.
Global AI capex correction as the principal downside risk to Japan.
vol_and_positioning: VIX remains elevated and correlations are rising. S&P dispersion over 2W is at the 30th percentile vs 5Y, single-name vol at the 81st percentile and the sector vs within-sector dispersion ratio at the 48th percentile.

US L/S net leverage is 41% (6th percentile since 2010) and gross 195%. Funds are net short Momentum for the first time since April 2025. Nets may fall below 40%, near COVID and Liberation Day lows of about 30-35%.
European gross leverage is 176% (84th percentile over 1Y). Asia gross leverage is 121%, at 5-year lows, with Semis, Hardware and Internet about 75% of supply.
Global Risk Demand Index at -2.4SD (Fear), the 8th Fear signal in 3M.
November MTD: Americas L/S -1.6% vs S&P -5.3%, Europe L/S -1.3% vs SXXP -1.2%, Asia L/S -2.9% vs MSCI APAC -6.5%.
Buybacks and month-end rebalancing could offer relief, but further systematic selling remains a risk.
geopolitical: New US export controls on advanced AI chips and overseas computing access are tighter than markets expected, affecting Chinese compute access and Southeast Asia data centers.
French elections and related fiscal risks are flagged for European equities and French banks.
Energy price spikes are flagged as a risk for Europe.

tension_points.bull_case: Corporates sound constructive, earnings revisions breadth is positive, activity data is resilient, and positioning is light enough for a sharp rebound. Wilson sees the correction as an entry point.
tension_points.bear_case: Selling has spread beyond Tech, investors pay up for safety, and prices have diverged from earnings expectations. Systematic selling and false dawns could persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fed path not repricing lower from 62bps of hikes, with US L/S nets falling below 40% toward 30-35% lows.
